record.original_question: Are all families of cyclic codes asymptotically bad, or do there exist asymptotically good cyclic linear codes?

evidence.quote: Whether or not there exist good linear codes which are also cyclic remains an open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over a fixed finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. A linear code of length $n$ and dimension $k$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is a $k$-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$; its minimum distance $d(C)$ is the minimum Hamming weight of a nonzero codeword. The code $C$ is called cyclic if it is invariant under the cyclic shift $(c_0, c_1, \dots, c_{n-1}) \mapsto (c_{n-1}, c_0, \dots, c_{n-2})$.

An infinite family $\{C_i\}_{i \ge 1}$ of linear codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$, with parameters $[n_i, k_i, d_i]$ and $n_i \to \infty$, is called asymptotically good if
$$\liminf_{i \to \infty} \frac{k_i}{n_i} > 0 \quad\text{and}\quad \liminf_{i \to \infty} \frac{d_i}{n_i} > 0.$$
Otherwise it is called asymptotically bad.

Question: Does there exist an asymptotically good family of cyclic linear codes over some finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, or is every infinite family of cyclic linear codes (over every fixed finite field) asymptotically bad?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the class of cyclic codes is asymptotically good is a long-standing open problem in coding theory and remains unresolved as of 2024. Partial results show certain subclasses (e.g., BCH codes, cyclic codes whose lengths use only finitely many primes) are asymptotically bad, while various generalized/additive cyclic code variants (Z_4Z_4Z_4-additive cyclic, SR-additive cyclic, F_2[u]F_2[u]-additive cyclic) have been shown to be asymptotically good. The original question for ordinary cyclic codes is still open.

status_evidence.title: Is the class of cyclic codes asymptotically good?
status_evidence.snippet: It is a long-standing open problem in coding theory whether there exists an asymptotically good sequence of cyclic codes.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of existence of asymptotically good cyclic codes is long-standing and open.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotically Good Additive Cyclic Codes Exist
status_evidence.snippet: Additive cyclic codes (a broader class) shown to be asymptotically good, while the analogous question for ordinary cyclic codes remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists for generalized/additive variants, but the original question is still open.

status_evidence.title: Z4Z4Z4-additive cyclic codes are asymptotically good
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs asymptotically good families of Z4Z4Z4-additive cyclic codes.
status_evidence.claim: Variants of cyclic codes are asymptotically good, but standard cyclic case remains open.
